<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d5787abe5ca3f1e6d582818d97636f7073bdf622` — the merge of head `22c7afb9a2ea30838c018a565bec6db7ed6178b2` into base `8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d5787abe5ca3f1e6d582818d97636f7073bdf622 && git checkout d5787abe5ca3f1e6d582818d97636f7073bdf622
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e 22c7afb9a2ea30838c018a565bec6db7ed6178b2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e && git merge --no-ff 22c7afb9a2ea30838c018a565bec6db7ed6178b2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-ui.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-installed-ui-entry.pin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/canonical-expression-envelopes.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts, packages/cli/test/platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/zh-CN.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/ja-JP.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/es-ES.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/zh-CN.source-hashes.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/ja-JP.source-hashes.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/es-ES.source-hashes.ts + .changeset/23933-installed-apps-packages-filter.md (the prose face, read for ②), packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts, packages/cloud-connection/package.json (the `exports` map), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (the `kernel:ready` registration, main `:687`), packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts (`ComponentNavItemSchema`, `:660-666`), packages/lint/src/validate-nav-target-refs.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts (`nav_packages`, `:51`), packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts (`pages`, `:1093`), packages/cli/scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs (`:393`), packages/qa/dogfood/test/platform-app-object-entry-views.test.ts (`:147`), docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json (`:1951-1999`), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs; objectui at the pinned `5e15928b4631`: packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/packageSource.ts, packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackagesPage.tsx (`:1118`), packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx (`resolveHref`, `:935-`), packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx (`:32`), packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/MarketplaceRowActions.tsx

Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run here; the objectui pin was read with `git show` at `5e15928b4631` (`9d857c998c`, objectui#12675's merge, is its ancestor — `is-ancestor` exit 0, re-measured).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept sets — none move. The diff touches no `packages/spec` path, no Zod schema, no HTTP door and no governed path; nothing the runtime accepts from an author changes. Right.

Public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

- **D1 — the entry's target, `page` to `component`.** `nav_marketplace_installed` becomes `{ type: 'component', componentRef: 'developer:packages', params: { source: 'marketplace' } }`, label and icon unchanged. `ComponentNavItemSchema` (`app.zod.ts:660-666`) declares `componentRef: z.string()` and `params: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()`, so the shape is on-spec; `validate-nav-target-refs` treats `component` as a non-rule (an unregistered ref renders a named diagnostic) and `url` as "external by definition", so the `component` spelling over the suggested `url` one is the right type for a first-party console component, and it is the spelling Setup's own `nav_packages` already uses on the same `developer:packages` (`setup-nav.contributions.ts:51`). At the pin, `packageSource.ts` declares `PACKAGES_SOURCE_PARAM = 'source'` and `PACKAGE_SOURCES = ['code', 'marketplace', 'authored']`, `PackagesPage.tsx:1118` reads `searchParams.getAll(PACKAGES_SOURCE_PARAM)` through `readSourceFilter` (an unknown or repeated value is refused by name), and `resolveHref`'s `component` branch serialises a nav item's `params` as the query string — so the entry opens `/apps/APP/component/developer/packages?source=marketplace`, the card's pin 2. The new pin test reads the entry back from a real kernel's metadata protocol after the plugin's own `kernel:ready` registration, with the plugin-absent control and a positive control (`nav_cloud_connection`) in the same group. Right.
- **D2 — the page retirement.** Ruling B item 2 retires the separate view "once the filtered view serves its actions". At the pin `MarketplaceRowActions.tsx` carries exactly Details and Uninstall on a marketplace row (Uninstall on local installs, shown with `features.installLocal` to a workspace admin), and `InstalledListWidget.tsx:32` only redirects to `packagesHref(basePath, 'marketplace')`; the old list carried those same two actions (H2's correction is a reading of objectui, not a new claim). The condition holds, so dropping `MarketplaceInstalledPage` and the bundle's `pages` key is the ruled move. `MarketplaceInstalledPage` was a module-level export never re-exported from `index.ts` and the package's `exports` map has only `.`, so no published export NAME leaves. Right.
- **D3 — the exported bundle's declared shape narrows.** `MARKETPLACE_INSTALLED_UI_BUNDLE` is exported from the package entry (`index.ts:82`, unchanged). Its value type loses the `pages` member and its nav item drops `pageName` for `componentRef` + `params`. A TypeScript consumer reading `MARKETPLACE_INSTALLED_UI_BUNDLE.pages` stops compiling; the three in-repo readers (the cli parity test, the envelope gate, the dogfood composition — the last reads only the manifest) are updated or unaffected. The change itself is right and is the ruling's consequence; what is **wrong** is how the changeset classifies it — see ②.
- **D4 — the wire narrows.** `GET /api/v1/meta/page` stops listing `marketplace_installed` and `/apps/setup/page/marketplace_installed` opens nothing; a stored favourite, recent item or bookmark on that address breaks (the changeset's own "What to do" line prescribes the new address, and the dev lists it as an acceptance note). The retirement is ruled and right; the classification is the same ② finding.
- **D5 — the bundle's own `version`, `0.2.0` to `0.3.0`, and its `description`.** Nothing in the repo pins the manifest id with a version (0 hits outside the file and the CHANGELOG), and the shape of the bundle did change. Right.
- **D6 — the translation bundle.** `pages.marketplace_installed` leaves `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES` and its two rows leave each `*.source-hashes.ts`; `nav_marketplace_installed` keeps all four labels. `TranslationData.pages` is `z.record(...)` (`translation.zod.ts:1093`), so this is a value removal keyed to a page that no longer exists, not a type change; without it the `pages.*` parity verdict reports an orphan. Right.
- **D7 — the gate populations.** `canonical-expression-envelopes.test.ts` keeps the two-way scan-equals-list check and moves its anti-vacuity floor 2 to 1; `platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts` moves its floors 5 to 4 and keeps the red-shape sample as a labelled fixture. Floors follow the population they guard; the equalities that give the verdict its teeth are untouched. Right. `vitest.config.ts` is a comment edit. Right.
- **D8 — untouched by design.** `MARKETPLACE_BROWSE_UI_BUNDLE`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` (the registration at `:687` still registers the bundle at `kernel:ready`, so no plugin, no entry — cloud ADR-0009 holds), `check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` (`:393` still passes the bundle into the nav roster; its line-54 comment is a historical measurement), and the spec's `marketplace:installed-list` row (the widget still exists and redirects at the pin; retiring the type pairs with objectui#12733 in the spec lane). Right, and each is inside the claim's hold-offs.
- **D9 — `content/docs`.** 0 hits for the page across `content/docs` outside releases, with 54 files carrying the control word `marketplace` (re-measured at `origin/main`). The card's docs clause is satisfied with no docs change. Right.

### ② Semver level

**The changeset's level and `Clause-②:` line do not match what the diff publishes — this is the FAIL.**

The committed `.changeset/23933-installed-apps-packages-filter.md` grades `@objectstack/cloud-connection` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` `patch` and declares `Clause-②: no` with no arm; the PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no`. `no` is true (nothing widens). But the diff narrows a published surface in two places the repo's own vocabulary names: a member of an exported declaration leaves (`MARKETPLACE_INSTALLED_UI_BUNDLE.pages`, D3 — `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`'s `runtime-export-retired` category exists exactly for "a retired member of an exported type" that "declares breaking truthfully"), and a served metadata page leaves the wire (D4), for which the changeset itself writes a consumer prescription. `clause2-line.mjs` defines the arm so that a diff which "NARROWS a published accept set answers `no` truthfully — and a narrowing is a breaking change"; AGENTS.md: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, and a breaking changeset carries its migration and exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker. The precedents in `packages/cloud-connection/CHANGELOG.md` (18.0.0-next.1 to next.3) spell this class `fix(...)!:` + `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + a marker, at `minor` (the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces: breaking ships as `minor`, never `major`). Option A's argument — the constant is an output and its readers are in-repo tests — is a statement about who is known to read it, not about what the package publishes; the d.ts and the metadata wire are both published.

What must change (a patch round can carry it verbatim):

1. `.changeset/23933-installed-apps-packages-filter.md` line 2: `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': minor` (line 3, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, may stay `patch` — the fixed group versions in lockstep — or move to `minor` with it; either is right).
2. Same file line 6: `feat(cloud-connection)!: Setup's "Installed Apps" entry opens Setup › Packages filtered to marketplace installs, and the separate Installed Apps page is no longer shipped` — the `!` is the precedent spelling for a declared-breaking summary.
3. Same file line 8: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`.
4. Same file, body: add exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker, as the HTML comment the gate's header prints — `adr-0087: not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/cloud-connection#MARKETPLACE_INSTALLED_UI_BUNDLE.pages) ...` followed by the why: the retired operand is a member of a published runtime export whose break reaches a TypeScript consumer through the compiler; the page it carried was plugin-registered in-memory metadata at `kernel:ready`, never a stored row, no spec key, authorable spelling or stored shape moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite. Beside it, one rewrite line naming exactly that operand, in the arrow form the category reads: `- \`MARKETPLACE_INSTALLED_UI_BUNDLE.pages\` -> delete` (the bundle carries no page; its entry is read from `navigationContributions`). Keep the existing "What to do" sentence for the retired page address as plain prose (it is the FROM-to-TO mapping AGENTS.md asks for, and it carries no arrow or table for the detector to read as a second prescription). The gate re-verifies the category's three predicates on its run; if it refuses, its text names the next step — `registered` would need a spec-lane conversion entry, which the claim holds off and the facts do not call for.
5. PR #24200 body line 3: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — `Check Changeset` and the queue guard read the body's line against the changeset's.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (H3, keep `no` or `no (narrowing)`): B.** Answered in ②, with the exact edits.
- **Open question 2 (surface breach in `867b780a1`: amend or drop the retirement): A.** The eight files (the four locale files, the three `*.source-hashes.ts`, the cli parity test) are forced by a retirement the ruling orders and the pin measures as served; they are mechanical, isolated in one commit and declared. The claim's file surface is amended by the seat, not by this record; dropping the retirement (B) would ship a page that only redirects, against ruling B item 2.
- **Route differs from the PM's suggestion (`component`, not `url`): right**, for the reasons in D1; the suggestion was a hint on the claim, not the ruling.
- **H2 corrected (Details and Uninstall, not update/uninstall/reseed/purge): read and confirmed at the pin** (`MarketplaceRowActions.tsx` header; the sample-data menu lives on the package page Details opens). The ruling's retirement condition is about the view's own actions, and those are served.
- **Pre-push refusal, amended unpublished commit; gate-runner timeouts with re-runs; the objectui ref fetched into `refs/os-dev/...` and deleted; `origin/main` moved under the worktree and was not merged (the diff is read here against merge base `2bcaefba9`, 13 files):** process notes, none leaves a mark in the diff.
- **Two stray `*.pid` files at the dev container's filesystem root:** outside the repository; nothing in the tree.
- **`test:repo` not run locally:** CI's `Test Core` is the verdict — all six shards and the aggregate concluded `success` on this head.
- **Out-of-scope findings, carrier none, noted not filed:** the stale QA text in `platform-core.json` (its `source` line and step 3 describe the retired page; the anchor resolves and the steps still execute against the filtered list) is a `domain:devx` prose fix and not a defect under Prime Directive #10 — a note is the right carrier; the spec's `marketplace:installed-list` row pairs with objectui#12733; the sidebar-highlight tie is an inference, not measured, and is the same for either spelling; the broken saved links are D4 and are the ② finding. The #23803 item-4 arithmetic (40, not 39, under ruling B) is for whichever card lands last.
- **Check-runs on `4013e2b0d`, all concluded at posting:** 40 runs, 34 `success`, 6 `skipped` (the opt-in and full-battery jobs), 0 failed — Build Core, the seven `Test Core` runs, the five type-check lanes (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger, TypeScript Type Check), the eight Lint lanes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the four claim guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Auto Label, and Check Changeset. Check Changeset is green against the `no`/`patch` declaration as written, which is consistent with ②: the gates grade the declaration they are given, and the arm is what makes the ADR-0087 gate ask for the marker. The PASS a patch round earns needs every check green on its own head.

### ① Derived judgments
